checklist.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Is P256VERIFY precompile gas consumption exactly 6900 for ALL execution paths?

reachability.notes: Gas consumption is deterministic and observable. Variable gas cost would be a consensus bug as different clients might disagree on remaining gas.

checklist.test_procedure: 1. Identify the P256VERIFY precompile implementation (address 0x100 per EIP-7212). 2. Construct test cases for ALL execution paths: (a) Empty input, (b) Malformed input (wrong length), (c) Invalid signature format, (d) Valid format but verification failure, (e) Successful verification. 3. For each test case, measure exact gas consumed by the precompile call. 4. Verify that ALL paths charge exactly 6900 gas - no more, no less. 5. Compare gas behavior across different client implementations (geth, nethermind, besu, erigon, reth) to ensure consensus. 6. Check for any early-exit code paths that might return before charging full gas. 7. Verify gas metering occurs at entry point, not conditionally based on validation results.
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-0003, Trust Boundary: tb-002, Invariant: EIP7951-SG006-INV-001. Variable gas consumption would cause network split as clients would disagree on remaining gas for subsequent operations.

checklist.title: Verify P256VERIFY gas charging occurs unconditionally at function entry

reachability.notes: Gas consumption is deterministic and observable. Variable gas cost would be a consensus bug as different clients might disagree on remaining gas.

checklist.test_procedure: 1. Review precompile implementation source code. 2. Verify that gas deduction (6900) happens BEFORE any input validation or early returns. 3. Check that no code path can exit the precompile without deducting exactly 6900 gas. 4. Look for conditional gas charging patterns that could vary based on input. 5. Ensure error handling paths also charge full gas before returning error. 6. Test with insufficient gas (< 6900) to verify proper out-of-gas handling.
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-0003, Supporting check for boundary integrity. Defensive check against implementation patterns where validation occurs before gas charging.
